review-pr.description: Reviews a Bitbucket pull request and posts findings + Jira cross-references. Usage: /review-pr <bitbucket-pr-url>
review-pr.template: Review the Bitbucket PR URL from $ARGUMENTS. Read .codex/skills/review-pr/SKILL.md and follow its fetch, exact-commit context review, completeness, and automatic publication workflow. Use fetchReviewData(url) to obtain the diff, snapshot, and reviewPrompt. Explain Changes from source PR in 1–5 evidence-backed bullets before the review result. Prepare {snapshot, status: complete or incomplete, limitations: string[], findings: ReviewFinding[]} and publish through publishReview(url, review) from src/review-pr/publication.ts, or the documented CLI with --json. Never use a bare findings array or bypass the snapshot check with low-level post functions. Missing context or a truncated diff requires an incomplete verdict, not NO ISSUES FOUND. Publishing updates marked comments for the authenticated author; only explicit Jira targets are used and no Jira status is changed. Inspect all destination results and report failures, limitations, and unrun checks accurately. No findings is not merge approval.

edit-ticket.description: Updates an existing Jira ticket's summary, description, or assignee. Usage: /edit-ticket <issue-key> [summary: <text>] [description: <text>] [assign: <name>]
edit-ticket.template:
You are a Jira ticket editor for configured Jira project (from JIRA_PROJECT_KEY env). The user provides an issue key and fields to update.

Instructions:
1. From $ARGUMENTS, parse:
   - The issue key (e.g. KAIRA-363)
   - Optional fields: summary, description, assign (by name)
2. Call the workflow:
   - `import { loadJiraConfig } from './src/review-pr/index.ts'`
   - `import { editTicketWorkflow } from './src/edit-ticket/index.ts'`
   - `const config = loadJiraConfig()`
   - `const result = await editTicketWorkflow(config, { issueKey, summary?, description?, assigneeName? })`
3. Send the result back to the user with the issue key and what was updated.

Only include fields that the user explicitly wants to change. If you generate a new description, you can use `formatDescription(issueType, description)` from `./src/create-ticket/index.ts` to wrap it in a template.
Mermaid descriptions retain their source and upload SVG attachments. Attachment permission is required. If creation enrichment fails, inspect the existing issue key in the error and edit it rather than creating a duplicate. Edits enrich before updating fields; uploaded attachments may remain on later failure. Repeated edits upload new attachments. Diagram layout is approximate; live Jira inline display is unverified.

create-ticket.description: Creates a Jira ticket (Task/Bug/Story/Epic) with an auto-improved summary and a structured, type-specific description. Supports linking children to an Epic via 'epic: KAIRA-XXX'. Usage: /create-ticket <work-type>: <description> [epic: KAIRA-XXX]
create-ticket.template:
# Create Ticket

Use the repository CLI from the repository directory. Load configured credentials through the CLI; never expose credentials or copy secrets into a ticket.

```bash
npx openpm-tools create-ticket "<improved summary>" --description "<complete description>" --story-points <estimate> [flags] --json
```

## Prepare the ticket

Rewrite the summary as a concise, professional action and affected feature. Preserve product names, technical identifiers, and prefixes such as [BE] or [FE]. Use the user's explicit issue type; otherwise choose Bug for a defect, Story for user-facing functionality, Epic for a multi-ticket initiative, and Task for other work.

Extract the requested assignee, sprint, parent epic, and estimate. Supported flags are `--type`, `--description`, `--assignee`, `--assignee-id`, `--sprint`, `--epic`, and `--story-points`. Use an exact Jira display name or a known account ID. Do not guess an account ID. If a name has no unique exact match, resolve it with available Jira read tools or ask for clarification before creating.

## Write a description the assignee can work from

Always prepare the clearest description the available context supports. Use supplied documents and relevant conversation context, preserving business rules, field mappings, URLs, payloads, and examples. Do not invent endpoint contracts, observed errors, designs, or approved business decisions.

Write a complete, structured description using Jira headings (`h3. Heading`) or Markdown headings. The CLI preserves supplied content without adding sections or inferred requirements.

Include the sections that help explain this ticket:
- Objective and context: the problem, affected product or users, and intended outcome.
- Scope and expected behavior: specific changes and relevant success, empty, validation, and error scenarios.
- Acceptance criteria: observable outcomes that can be tested; avoid vague criteria such as "works correctly".
- Technical details and examples: known endpoints, payloads, mappings, dependencies, and related tickets.
- Open questions and assumptions: label unresolved decisions and estimation assumptions explicitly.

For Bugs, include known actual/expected behavior, reproduction steps, environment, and evidence. Mark unavailable evidence as unknown rather than manufacturing reproduction steps. For Stories, explain user benefit. For Epics, explain goals and child work streams.

A short request still needs a concrete objective, known scope, and useful acceptance criteria. State material unknowns clearly. Ask only when an unresolved choice would materially change the requested work. An omitted description is a CLI fallback skeleton, not a finished ticket.

## Recommend and populate story points

Preserve an explicit user estimate. Otherwise recommend an estimate from the ticket's scope, complexity, components, integration dependencies, testing, and uncertainty, then pass it through `--story-points`. Use the project's known scale. If none is available, use 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, or 13 as a provisional Fibonacci scale:
- 1: isolated, well-understood change with limited testing.
- 2: small change with a few validation paths.
- 3: moderate feature or defect affecting a familiar flow.
- 5: several components or an integration with meaningful testing.
- 8: substantial integration, cross-system changes, or notable uncertainty.
- 13: broad work needing decomposition; explain the recommendation and identify child work without creating extra tickets unless requested.

Points represent relative effort and uncertainty, not hours. Include a brief estimation rationale and material assumptions in the description. Do not silently assign 0 for missing context. For an Epic, explain whether its estimate covers the whole initiative and avoid presenting it as a sprint commitment. The CLI requires a finite, non-negative estimate and does not infer one.

## Sprint and completion

An explicit sprint must exist on the selected board. Otherwise, the CLI uses the active sprint, then the first future sprint, or leaves the issue in the backlog if neither exists. Epics do not enter sprints; omit `--sprint` for them.

Check the saved ticket with an available Jira read tool when possible: summary, description, type, assignee, story points, parent epic, and sprint. If a read tool is unavailable, report the CLI result and state that saved fields were not independently verified. Return the issue link, summary, assignee, actual sprint or backlog placement, and estimate with a short rationale.

If any creation step errors, the issue may already exist. Inspect the issue key in the error or locate the issue in Jira before retrying. Repair the existing issue when creation succeeded but sprint assignment or diagram enrichment failed. Never blindly repeat create after an uncertain response.

## Mermaid Descriptions

Keep Mermaid source in fenced `mermaid` or `{code:mermaid}` blocks without changing the supplied diagram logic. The shared Jira client renders and uploads SVG attachments while retaining source. Attachment permission is required. Creation saves the source first; an enrichment failure reports the existing issue key. Edit that issue instead of retrying creation. Edits enrich before updating fields; uploaded attachments may remain on later failure. Repeated edits upload new attachments. Layout measurements are approximate; live Jira inline display is unverified.

User request: $ARGUMENTS

sprint-report.description: Generates a rich Sprint Report from Jira (completion rate, scope-change rate, carryover, story points, burndown, health scorecard, blockers, and auto-generated best-practice insights) for the current active sprint or a specified sprint. Supports HTML export. Usage: /sprint-report [sprint-name-or-number] [export]
sprint-report.template:
You are a Sprint Report agent for Jira configured Jira project (from JIRA_PROJECT_KEY env).

Instructions:
1. Parse the argument from $ARGUMENTS:
   - If empty: report on the current active sprint
   - If provided and not the word 'export': use as sprint name/ID to search for
   - Detect an `export` flag: if the user says 'export' or passes `export` anywhere in the arguments, set exportHtml to a path under the current working directory.
2. Call the workflow:
   - `import { loadJiraConfig, runFromEnv } from './src/sprint-report/index.ts'`
   - If export was requested:
     `const result = await runFromEnv({ sprintName: '<parsed-arg-or-undefined>', exportHtml: process.cwd() + '/sprint-report-<sanitized-sprint-name>.html' })`
     (sanitize the sprint name by replacing non-alphanumerics with '-'; if the sprint name is unknown yet, you may use a placeholder and the workflow will derive the filename from the resolved sprint name when given a directory)
   - Otherwise:
     `const result = await runFromEnv({ sprintName: '<parsed-arg-or-undefined>' })`
3. Return the Markdown report to the user as-is. The report already ends with an 'Insights & Suggestions' section — surface those insights prominently (you may quote them at the top as a TL;DR). If HTML export was requested, the returned markdown includes a line noting where the HTML report was written.

If the sprint is not found, return a clear error message.

release-workflow.description: Creates an unreleased Jira release/version for all tickets in the current sprint with status Ready for Release, assigns the version to them, and generates release notes (markdown file + Jira version description). Usage: /release-workflow [version-name]
release-workflow.template:
Read docs/document-writing.md and docs/document-diagrams.md for the generated report or release notes. You are a Jira release workflow automation agent for configured Jira project (from JIRA_PROJECT_KEY env).

Instructions:
1. Parse the argument from $ARGUMENTS:
   - If empty: pass undefined to use auto-generated name (Release YYYY-MM-DD)
   - If provided: pass as versionName
2. Call the workflow:
   - `import { loadJiraConfig, runFromEnv } from './src/release-workflow/index.ts'`
   - `const result = await runFromEnv({ versionName: '<arg-or-undefined>' })`
3. Report summary to user:
   - Version Name
   - Version ID
   - Ticket count
   - Release notes path

If runFromEnv throws an error, report the error clearly.

daily-standup.description: Generates a markdown daily standup report from recent Jira activities (Yesterday's Progress, Today's Focus, Risks & Blockers). Usage: /daily-standup [assigneeName]
daily-standup.template: Follow instructions in .opencode/command/daily-standup.md to generate the daily standup report. Arguments: $ARGUMENTS

create-prdd.description: Creates one English nine-section PRDD in Notion or Obsidian from source evidence and focused questions.
create-prdd.template: Read docs/notion-workflow.md when DOCUMENTS_PROVIDER=notion. Read docs/document-writing.md and docs/document-diagrams.md. Follow instructions in .opencode/command/create-prdd.md to inspect sources, ask focused questions, and generate one English PRDD. Arguments: $ARGUMENTS

brainstorm.description: Runs a topic-agnostic brainstorming interview and exports one collision-safe Markdown file. Usage: /brainstorm [topic] [--quick|--deep] [--out <directory>]
brainstorm.template: Read docs/notion-workflow.md when DOCUMENTS_PROVIDER=notion. Read docs/document-writing.md and docs/document-diagrams.md. Follow instructions in .opencode/command/brainstorm.md to conduct the brainstorming interview and export one Markdown file. Arguments: $ARGUMENTS

edit-prdd.description: Edits/updates an existing Product Requirements & Design Document (PRDD) in your configured document workspace (`PRDD - <Name> (EN).md`). Usage: /edit-prdd [product-name]
edit-prdd.template: Read docs/notion-workflow.md when DOCUMENTS_PROVIDER=notion. Read docs/document-writing.md and docs/document-diagrams.md. Follow instructions in .opencode/command/edit-prdd.md to locate and update the English PRDD from source evidence. Arguments: $ARGUMENTS

extract-knowledge.description: Extract document files (.docx, .pdf, .pptx, .xlsx, .md, .csv) into AI-friendly knowledge markdown in Notion or Obsidian vault. Usage: /extract-knowledge <file-or-folder> [--llm] [--out <dir>] [--overwrite] [--vault <path>] [--json]
extract-knowledge.template: Read docs/notion-workflow.md when DOCUMENTS_PROVIDER=notion. Read docs/document-writing.md and docs/document-diagrams.md. Follow instructions in .opencode/command/extract-knowledge.md to extract knowledge files. Arguments: $ARGUMENTS
